name: Physician Assistant
description: Diagnosing, managing and prescribing across essentially every specialty — $135,880 median, 162,700 employed, 12,000 openings a year, growing much faster than average. ⚠⚠⚠ The barrier is not the transcript. PAEA puts the median matriculant at about 3,200 hours of direct patient contact — one to three years of clinical work BEFORE the programme starts — and Florida's six public programmes award 225 master's degrees a year between them. ⚠⚠ So the real question this page answers is: which job do you take first?
credentialNote: ⚠⚠ FLORIDA WROTE THE CREDENTIAL ESCALATION INTO STATUTE WITH A DATE. Under s. 458.347, F.S., an applicant must have completed a programme accredited by the Accreditation Review Commission on Education for the Physician Assistant (ARC-PA) and passed the National Commission on Certification of Physician Assistants examination — and anyone MATRICULATING AFTER 31 DECEMBER 2020 must hold a master's degree. ⚠ Check a programme's ARC-PA STATUS, not merely that it has one: accreditation comes as provisional, continued or probationary, and the difference matters to your eligibility and to employers. ⚠⚠⚠ AND THE SAME STATUTE CAPS HOW MANY OF YOU A PHYSICIAN CAN EMPLOY. A physician may not supervise more than 10 currently licensed physician assistants at any one time, and supervision means the physician's easy availability or physical presence for consultation and direction, which may be by telecommunication. ⚠ Prescribing is delegated by the supervising physician against a council formulary, with Schedule II controlled substances limited to a 7-DAY SUPPLY and paediatric psychiatric medication to 14 days. ⚠ A PA may authenticate any document a physician may — including death certificates, do-not-resuscitate orders and school physicals — which is a broader authority than most people assume. ⚠⚠ Let a licence lapse for four years or more and you must retake the entry-level examination, so plan career breaks around that.
bodyHtml:
⚠⚠⚠ The admission barrier is a JOB, and this site can tell you which one

PAEA's Student Report puts matriculating PA students at a median of about 3,200 hours of direct patient contact — 25th percentile near 1,750, 75th near 5,600. Grade point averages cluster near 3.6.

⚠⚠⚠ Read those two facts together: the GPA screens you out and the HOURS get you in. Three thousand two hundred hours is roughly eighteen months to two years of full-time clinical work before the programme begins. Almost nobody plans for it early enough, and the people who do are the ones who get in.

So the practical question is which job to take. Florida's options, shortest first:

RouteTrainingFL public institutionsMedian wage
✅ Phlebotomist⚠⚠ under 12 weeks29$45,230
EMTabout one semester⚠ 39 (widest in the state)—
Medical assistant~1,300 clock hours38$45,690
Paramedicassociate degree39—
Surgical technologistassociate degree25—
Respiratory therapistassociate or baccalaureate——
Registered nurseassociate degree——

⚠⚠ Every one of these has its own page on this site, so you can compare them properly rather than taking the first thing a pre-PA advisor mentions.

⚠⚠⚠ But check the definition before you enrol in anything. Most programmes distinguish direct patient care experience — hands-on and responsible — from general healthcare experience such as scribing or reception, and count them differently or not at all. Get each programme's own wording in writing. A year spent accumulating hours that do not count is the most expensive mistake available on this path.

⚠⚠⚠ The comparison that actually matters: PA or nurse practitioner?

These two careers are chosen against each other constantly, and the honest comparison is in the statutes, not the job descriptions.

Physician assistantAutonomous APRN
Florida statutes. 458.347s. 464.0123
Independence⚠ supervised — a supervising physician is required✅ autonomous after 3,000 supervised clinical hours plus graduate credits in differential diagnosis and pharmacology
Clinical scope✅ every specialty — surgery, emergency, dermatology, orthopaedics⚠ primary care only — family medicine, general paediatrics, general internal medicine; no surgery beyond subcutaneous procedures
Employer constraint⚠⚠ a physician may supervise at most 10 PAs at one timenone once registered

⚠⚠⚠ The trade is real and it runs in both directions. The autonomous APRN buys independence and pays for it in scope: primary care only. The PA buys scope — the whole of medicine and surgery — and pays for it in independence.

⚠ And the ten-PA cap is a supply fact nobody explains. The number of PA posts a practice can create is tied to its physician headcount in a way nurse practitioner posts are not. It does not make jobs scarce — 12,000 openings a year says otherwise — but it shapes where they are.

The occupation

Physician assistants (29-1071)
2025 median$135,880
Employed (2024)162,700
Annual openings12,000
Growth 2024–34✅ much faster than average (7% or higher)
Education81% master's, 14% professional degree, 5% bachelor's

O*NET's task list is worth reading for what it does not hedge: make tentative diagnoses and decisions about management and treatment of patients; interpret diagnostic test results for deviations from normal; prescribe therapy or medication with physician approval; examine patients to obtain information about their physical condition.

⚠ This is clinical decision-making, not assistance. The title understates the job, which is part of why the profession keeps arguing about its own name.

⚠⚠ Six programmes, 225 seats

InstitutionMaster's awarded (2023)
University of Florida58
Florida State University56
University of South Florida47
Florida International University45
Florida Gulf Coast University19

⚠ All master's, all universities, and all in the south and centre of the state plus Gainesville and Tallahassee. There is no state-college route and no part-time undergraduate route.

⚠⚠ One honest caveat: this site lists PUBLIC institutions only. Florida has several substantial private PA programmes, so 225 is not the state's whole annual output — but it is the whole of its public-tuition output, and that is the number that decides what this costs you.

✅ The prerequisite year is the cheap part — do it locally

The prerequisite list is consistent across programmes and Florida's public colleges carry every item of it, most at 15 to 39 institutions: anatomy and physiology with laboratories, microbiology, general chemistry, organic chemistry or biochemistry, general biology, statistics, psychology, developmental psychology, medical terminology and composition.

⚠⚠ So the sensible shape of this path is: do the prerequisites at a state college while working a clinical job, then apply to one of the six. That is cheaper than a four-year science degree taken without the hours, and it directly attacks the thing that actually decides admission.

⚠ Watch the science grades anyway. Programmes usually compute a separate science GPA, and a weak organic chemistry grade is visible for years.

Necessary skills

  • Differential diagnosis — generating and narrowing a list under uncertainty, which is the intellectual core of the job.
  • Pharmacology held in working memory, because prescribing is delegated to you and the formulary is not.
  • Procedural competence and the judgement to stop — suturing, injections, reductions, lines, and knowing which case is not yours.
  • Working inside someone else's licence. The supervising relationship is a professional skill, not a formality, and managing it well is what makes a career comfortable.
  • Speed without shortcuts in clinics and emergency departments that are always behind.
  • Stamina for a compressed programme. Two to three years, didactic then rotations, effectively full-time; almost nobody works through it.

Advice

⚠⚠⚠ Start accumulating patient care hours in your first year of college, not your last. Three thousand two hundred is the median, and you cannot compress it. This is the single most important sentence on this page.

⚠⚠ Get each programme's definition of qualifying hours in writing before you take the job. Scribe work and front-desk work frequently do not count; phlebotomy, EMS, medical assisting, nursing assistance and technologist work generally do.

⚠ Do the prerequisites at a state college. They are carried nearly everywhere in Florida, they cost a fraction of university tuition, and the admissions committee does not care where the credit came from nearly as much as it cares about the grade and the hours.

⚠⚠ Decide PA against nurse practitioner on scope and independence, not on salary. If you want surgery or emergency medicine, the PA route reaches them and autonomous APRN practice in Florida does not. If you want to run your own primary care practice, s. 464.0123 is the route and s. 458.347 is not.

And take the ten-PA supervision cap into account when you look at where the jobs are. Large groups and hospital systems can absorb many PAs; a two-physician practice can employ at most twenty, and in reality one or two.

programs.note: The programme itself — 6 Florida public institutions, 225 master's degrees a year, UF 58, FSU 56, USF 47, FIU 45, FGCU 19. ⚠ Read its degrees note on the patient-care-hours barrier and on checking ARC-PA accreditation STATUS rather than just its existence.

⚠⚠⚠ The alternative to weigh, and the difference is statutory. An APRN meeting s. 464.0123 may practise AUTONOMOUSLY in Florida primary care; a PA under s. 458.347 may not practise without a supervising physician. ⚠ But the PA's scope reaches surgery, emergency and every specialty, and autonomous APRN practice does not. ⚠⚠ Nursing is also an excellent route to the hours: 78 Florida institutions.

⚠⚠⚠ The fastest route in Florida to being employed in patient contact — all 772 credentials awarded in 2023 were certificates of UNDER TWELVE WEEKS, at 29 public institutions. ⚠ Confirm with each PA programme that it counts phlebotomy as direct patient care; definitions vary, and this one sits nearer the line than nursing or EMS.
⚠⚠ The widest clinical footprint in Florida — 39 public institutions — and EMT is about a semester. Hands-on by definition, so the hours are rarely questioned. ⚠ The standard pre-PA job for a reason.

⚠ A broader hours route than phlebotomy, and the same programme: s. 458.3485 permits vital signs, venipuncture, injections and medication administration under physician supervision, and Florida's medical assisting framework contains the phlebotomy exit at 75 hours. 38 public institutions.

⚠ Named for applicants aiming at surgical PA practice specifically — a large part of the profession, and the part autonomous APRN practice cannot reach. Scrubbing cases produces unambiguous hands-on hours and directly relevant experience.

⚠ A slower route to the hours but a licensed clinical one, so they are never questioned and the pay while accumulating them is much better than an entry certificate. ⚠⚠ Worth considering if you are not certain about PA school: it is a career in its own right rather than a stepping stone.

courses.reason: Anatomy and Physiology I — 20 institutions. The universal PA prerequisite, and the grade admissions committees look at first.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Two equivalent packagings: BSC2085 plus BSC2085L at 20 institutions, combined BSC2085C at 7. ⚠⚠ Some programmes require the laboratory explicitly — check, because the combined form satisfies it and a bare lecture does not.

courses.reason: Anatomy and Physiology I Laboratory — 19 institutions. Required by most programmes as a separate line item.
Anatomy and Physiology II — 19 institutions. Cardiovascular, respiratory, renal and endocrine — the systems most of the clinical year is about.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Also carried as the combined BSC2086C at 7 institutions.

courses.reason: Anatomy and Physiology II Laboratory — 19 institutions.
Microbiology — 16 institutions. Universally required, and the foundation for infectious disease and antibiotic prescribing.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ MCB2010L, the laboratory, is carried at 15 and is separately required by most programmes.

courses.reason: General Chemistry I — 15 institutions. Required by essentially every programme, and the gateway to organic and biochemistry.
General Chemistry II — 15 institutions. The second half, and a prerequisite for organic chemistry.
Organic Chemistry I — 29 institutions. ⚠ Required by many but not all programmes; where a programme accepts biochemistry instead, biochemistry is usually the more useful course clinically.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Check each programme: some require organic, some biochemistry, some either. Taking the wrong one is a year lost.

courses.reason: ⚠ Biochemistry — only 7 institutions, and upper division, so it is the hardest prerequisite to obtain locally. Several programmes prefer or require it over organic chemistry.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ With seven carriers this is the prerequisite most likely to force a transfer or an online course. Check whether your target programmes accept organic chemistry instead BEFORE planning around it.

courses.reason: Elementary Statistics — 39 institutions. Universally required, and you will read trial evidence for the rest of your career.
Introduction to Psychology — 33 institutions. A standard prerequisite, and behavioural health is a large share of primary care practice.
Developmental Psychology — 29 institutions. Frequently required specifically, and often overlooked until the application year.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Check the requirement early; it is one of the commonest missing prerequisites.

courses.reason: General Biology I — 20 institutions. The majors-level biology sequence, required where a programme wants majors biology rather than anatomy alone.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Not interchangeable with BSC2085 at most programmes — they want both.

courses.reason: Medical Terminology — 16 institutions. Required by some programmes, assumed by all, and cheap.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Florida numbers this twice: HSC1531 at 16 institutions and HSC2531 at 8.

courses.reason: English Composition I — 39 institutions. A universal prerequisite, and the personal statement is a real component of the application.

Fundamentals of Speech Communication — 16 institutions. ⚠ Named because PA admission is interview-heavy, frequently in multiple mini-interview format, and this is the cheapest deliberate preparation available.

An APRN may register for AUTONOMOUS practice with an unencumbered licence, no discipline in five years, 3,000 clinical hours within five years under physician supervision, and 3 graduate semester hours each in differential diagnosis and pharmacology. ⚠ Scope is limited to PRIMARY CARE — family medicine, general paediatrics, general internal medicine — with no surgery except subcutaneous procedures.
